market_holds: Spot $20.02 (sealed baseline 2026-11-23 18:08 UTC). The option-implied event move is 10.46% (straddle 12.86% to the Dec-18 expiry, ATM spread 45% of mid, so this is indicative only). Over 7 prints the median reaction is 13.81% and 5 of 7 were down, including -13.81% on the Dec-2025 FY guide print and -14.55% on the Aug-2026 Q3 print. Run-in: -7.8% over 5 sessions and -10.0% over 20. The stock fell from $22.53 (Nov 13) to $19.27 (Nov 20), -14.5% (stockanalysis history), with Nov 20 volume at 1.13M against a 20-day average of about 415k (2.7x). The Russell 2000 was down roughly 3-5% over the same stretch, which leaves about 10 points specific to CMP. That selling coincides with NOAA's Nov 19 winter outlook, which leans warm for the Great Lakes in a forecast record-strength El Nino, after the 6th-warmest October on record in Chicago. The stock is 40% off its 52-week high and back to its post-August low. Q4 consensus is about -$0.01 EPS on about $221M revenue (Earnings Whispers preview, Nov 15). FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide is $218-242M (midpoint $230M); with 9M at $191.6M, the implied Q4 is about $38M (range $26-50M). I found no FY27 EBITDA consensus. Already public: highway bid-season price increases of about double digits with tight industry inventories, a lower committed FY27 highway volume, unresolved Goderich costs, the Canadian-salt tariff that ran Aug 19 to Sep 15, and a capital-allocation update and FY27 guide promised for this release. Short interest is about 1.7M shares, roughly 4-7% of float (dates Aug-Oct 2026, sources disagree).
view: This print turns on the FY27 guide, not the seasonally small Q4: salt EBITDA per ton, the committed highway volume, and Goderich cost and fuel assumptions, plus the promised capital-allocation update. The inputs pull both ways and each side is already visible to the market. The price side is strong and public: management said in August that 2026-27 contracts are up about double digits; public tenders (Mount Prospect +65%, a Pennsylvania COG +80%) and an Illinois state program where 250+ communities got no bids point to a tight market. My own rough arithmetic: about +10% on roughly 8M committed highway tons, less a 0.7M-ton volume step-down, gives a normal-weather FY27 guide plausibly above FY26's $230M. Against that, management's cost record is poor (salt guide cut twice in FY26, Goderich hoisting below plan, the mill project delayed), a month of tariff on Goderich shipments may hit Q4, and the weather is the obvious problem. A record-strength El Nino with NOAA leaning warm, a warm October and early November, and a Q1 comparison against last year's +43% highway volume quarter mean any normal-weather guide will be discounted, and the call (9am ET, before the scored open) will likely concede a slow start. The market has visibly moved on the weather: -14% in a week on heavy volume into the print, back to the August low and below JPMorgan's August underweight target of $27. That leaves the bar lower than the history of down reactions suggests, but I cannot see where the guide lands against an unpublished consensus. I have no dated, company-specific input that the price has not already met. Close to a coin flip with a large absolute move.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the FY27 EBITDA guide, and its inputs (double-digit contract pricing against lower committed volume, unresolved Goderich costs and a warm El Nino winter) are all public. The price has visibly reacted to the weather (-14% in the week into the print on 2.7x volume). I found no dated evidence that puts the guide clearly above or below what a $20 stock already implies, so neither side reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FY27 adjusted EBITDA guide midpoint clearly above about $260M, with salt per-ton margin expansion and a buyback, would favour up. A guide near or below FY26's $230M, or a weak-weather Q1 framing with Goderich costs still rising, would favour down.

self_critique: The case for up is stronger than 49 suggests if the normal-weather guide shows clear EBITDA growth (double-digit pricing on a tight market with supply exits), a buyback is announced, and the stock already discounts a mild winter after a 14% fall to its August low; a heavily sold name can bounce hard on any growth guide. The case for down: this management has disappointed on costs for a year, the Dec-2025 FY guide print fell 13.8%, and the 9am call will be asked about a warm start and a hard Q1 comparison. Neither side has dated evidence I can show the price lacks.
approach_notes: Taking the run-in apart against the tape (P6) and requiring proof of 'priced in' (P4) helped show the weather risk is in the price, not just in the news. P7's push to estimate the unseen line was hard to use without any public FY27 consensus to anchor the arithmetic against.
